name: Even Split
description: A revolution has recently happened in Segmentland. The new government is committed to equality, and they hired you to help with land redistribution in the country. Segmentland is a segment of length $$$l$$$ kilometers, with the capital in one of its ends. There are $$$n$$$ citizens in Segmentland, the home of $$$i$$$-th citizen is located at the point $$$a_i$$$ kilometers from the capital. No two homes are located at the same point. Each citizen should receive a segment of positive length with ends at integer distances from the capital that contains her home. The union of these segments should be the whole of Segmentland, and they should not have common points besides their ends. To ensure equality, the difference between the lengths of the longest and the shortest segments should be as small as possible.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \leq l \leq 10^9; 1 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \lt a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \dots \lt a_n \lt l$$$).
output_specification: Output $$$n$$$ pairs of numbers $$$s_i, f_i$$$ ($$$0 \leq s_i \lt f_i \leq l$$$), one pair per line. The pair on $$$i$$$-th line denotes the ends of the $$$[s_i, f_i]$$$ segment that $$$i$$$-th citizen receives. If there are many possible arrangements with the same difference between the lengths of the longest and the shortest segments, you can output any of them.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1666E — Even Split [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
